decisions.summary: Class 5 broadleaf-over-conifer sent to the glyph check as undecidable (no species on a crown)
decisions.why: Not undecidable: the recorded case (ledger 2026-09-28, 269 B30: broadleaf inked over earlier clumps' conifers) is draw order the renderer controls; rules-recon item 5 says it is decidable from the crowns' z-order and fills in the SVG, or the record can carry the species. 'The record lacks the field' is implementation cost. Sending a geometric draw-order defect to a check that fires only on an occasion leaves it unchecked on every engine change - the opposite of the request (fix the placer, then stop checking). Required: a rule (record species on tree_crowns, or read fills/z-order from the SVG, or draw conifers by construction in one order) proved red on the recorded case.

decisions.summary: Class 12 (drawn vs rolled area) ruled as 'drawn within its roll's own range'
decisions.why: The class compares drawn with ROLLED. Checking against the range the roll is drawn from passes Sawada's wood at 60% of its roll (10,672 of 17,692 sq ft), the one pool failure rules-recon item 12 measured - the rule loosened where the pool fails, which the plan's own B preamble forbids. Recon said decide target vs ceiling first; the plan decided it implicitly. Required: compare drawn with the rolled value (band GUESS) and fix the placer, or, if research shows the roll is a ceiling, record that finding and test drawn <= rolled and >= the floor, labeled as research-decided like D5.

decisions.summary: Class 14 (brook share off the frame) ruled as the brook crossing the view as one piece
decisions.why: The literal share is 0.37-0.67 on every correct map (canvas padding, brooks end off-canvas by construction), so it would fail correct maps; the recorded defect was the brook leaving and re-entering the view in three pieces (230 pass 3), which the one-piece predicate catches. The purpose survives.

decisions.summary: B4 (unlabeled): parallel-twin rule exempts siblings of one comb, governed instead by 'the comb's researched branch spacing'
decisions.why: The recorded case (ledger 2026-08-28, 'twin branch canals ~25 ft apart') and all four pool failures are comb siblings, so the carve-out excludes exactly the recorded case and the failing pool - the rule loosened where the pool fails. Rules-recon item 4: 'Norm: none found'; no branch spacing found in research/water. Required: the rule covers siblings and goes red on the recorded case, and the placer is fixed; only if a research pass FINDS a branch spacing that permits the pair is the class sent back through the audit as research-decided (FR-003's escape), recorded with the citation, and the sibling spacing then enforced by test.

decisions.summary: B14 (unlabeled): typed counts in the census block and dated history entries exempt from the agrees-with-manifest refusal
decisions.why: The census block is checked by the existing test; a dated entry states a past manifest's count and cannot truthfully agree with the current one, so the literal rule would force falsifying or deleting history the GM never asked to remove. Condition: an entry moved under a date must be genuinely historical, not a current claim relabeled.

decisions.summary: Audit MOVED rows B11 (Mode A notes counts vs data-kind census, ~15 fires) and Z5 residual (sized ink outside the size table) get no rule in plan B and no review in plan C
decisions.why: Silently dropped: R1 marks both MOVED (a new rule, US2), the MOVED list carries B11 as item 4, yet no B-item builds them and no contract keeps them. A check removed with no rule and no review is the opposite of 'fix the placement algorithm and THEN stop checking'. Required: a B-item for each (sheet notes counts against the data-kind census; size-table coverage of paths/circles/glyphs), or keep them in building-review/size-audit with the reason.
